Neighbor 1 is a fairly strong mutagenic analog despite one countervailing exposure-related feature. The query is lower in QED drug-likeness than the neighbor (0.274 vs 0.4382, delta -0.1642), which is consistent with the lower-drug-likeness side of the comparison leaning toward mutagenicity here. The query is also more lipophilic, with estimated logD rising from 4.8459 to 5.9954 (delta +1.1495), and in Ames settings very high lipophilicity can still matter operationally through exposure, but here that shift is treated as unfavorable for mutagenicity. More importantly, the query is one ring richer overall (ring count 5 vs 4, delta +1) and one aromatic carbocycle richer as well (5 vs 4, delta +1), and the comparison also notes the same phenol motif in both structures, so that shared hydroxylated aromatic chemistry does not separate them. The fraction of sp3 carbons is 0 in both molecules, preserving the flat, highly aromatic character. Taken together, the extra ring system and aromatic carbocycle content make this neighbor support the mutagenic class.

Neighbor 2 is also a mutagenic analog overall. It has a slightly higher QED drug-likeness than the query (0.341 vs 0.274, delta -0.067), which in this comparison still aligns with the mutagenic side. The query again has more ring system content, with ring count increasing from 4 to 5 (delta +1) and aromatic carbocycle count from 4 to 5 (delta +1), both of which favor the mutagenic interpretation because the query remains in the more fused-aromatic, more planar region. The fraction of sp3 carbons also drops from 0.0526 in the neighbor to 0 in the query (delta -0.0526), reinforcing the move toward a flatter aromatic scaffold. Against that, the query has a larger Labute surface area (132.9523 vs 116.6356, delta +16.3167) and higher estimated logD (5.9954 vs 5.1566, delta +0.8388), both of which can reduce effective bacterial exposure and therefore modestly argue against mutagenicity. Even so, the aromatic-ring expansion and more planar character dominate this pairwise comparison.

Neighbor 3 closely resembles Neighbor 1 and lands on the same side. The query again shows lower QED drug-likeness than the neighbor (0.274 vs 0.4382, delta -0.1642), a shift that in this local comparison aligns with the mutagenic label. The query is also more hydrophobic in estimated logD (5.9954 vs 4.8466, delta +1.1488), which is an exposure-relevant change but not enough to overturn the structural signal. As with Neighbor 1, the query has one more ring overall (5 vs 4, delta +1) and one more aromatic carbocycle (5 vs 4, delta +1), and both molecules share phenol and a fully sp3-depleted character with fraction of sp3 carbons at 0 in both cases. That combination again preserves the highly aromatic scaffold that is more consistent with the mutagenic analogs.

Neighbor 4 remains a mutagenic neighbor even though a couple of features point the other way. The query has more aromatic structure than the neighbor, with aromatic carbocycle count rising from 4 to 5 (delta +1), and the neighbor has 4 copies of benzene while the query has 5 (delta +1), both of which strengthen the same planar polyaromatic theme associated with mutagenicity. The query also has lower QED drug-likeness than the neighbor (0.274 vs 0.4382, delta -0.1642), which again tracks with the mutagenic side in this local context. The query has one additional ring as well (ring count 5 vs 4, delta +1). In the opposite direction, the query is more lipophilic (estimated logP 6.005 vs 4.8518, delta +1.1532) and heavier (heavy-atom count 23 vs 19, delta +4), both of which can limit soluble exposure in Ames and therefore lean against mutagenicity. But the much more aromatic, benzene-rich scaffold still makes this neighbor closer to the mutagenic class overall.

Neighbor 5 is another mutagenic analog, though it carries some exposure-limiting differences. The benzene count is matched at 5 in both molecules, so the aromatic core remains comparably dense. Ring count is also unchanged at 5, and aromatic carbocycle count is unchanged at 5, keeping the scaffold firmly in the polyaromatic region. QED drug-likeness is slightly higher in the query than the neighbor (0.274 vs 0.2302, delta +0.0438), but that does not break the overall resemblance. The query also contains phenol once whereas the neighbor has none, which is a local difference that in this comparison leans away from mutagenicity. On the other hand, the query has a measurable topological polar surface area of 20.23 while the neighbor is at 0 (delta +20.23), a shift that increases polarity and can reduce passive exposure. Even with those two counterweights, the matched high aromaticity and ring density keep this neighbor aligned with the mutagenic set.

Neighbor 6 provides the strongest mutagenic support of the six. The query has far more benzene units than the neighbor (5 vs 1, delta +4), and it also has much greater ring content overall (5 vs 1, delta +4) and aromatic carbocycle count (5 vs 1, delta +4). The query is lower in QED drug-likeness than the neighbor (0.274 vs 0.4907, delta -0.2168), which again fits the mutagenic side in this local comparison. Although the query is much larger in heavy-atom count (23 vs 8, delta +15), and larger size can sometimes reduce exposure in bacterial assays, that same point is outweighed by the dramatic increase in aromatic surface and ring density. The query is also slightly less neutral at the configured pH (neutral fraction 0.9781 vs 0.9968, delta -0.0187), a small shift toward greater ionization that can further affect exposure. Overall, this neighbor is much closer to the mutagenic aromatic cluster than to the small nonmutagenic reference.

Across the positive neighbors, the query repeatedly tracks with more fused aromatic content, more rings, and lower QED than the mutagenic analogs, while the higher logD, surface area, and heavy-atom count are mainly exposure modifiers rather than clear protective features. Across the negative neighbors, the query is consistently more aromatic and ring-rich, with more benzene units and more aromatic carbocycles, and those structural-alert-like features outweigh the countervailing size or polarity effects. Taken together, the six comparisons most strongly support option (B): is mutagenic.
